segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:25
segments.html:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם
הַזָּן אֶת הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ בְּטוּבוֹ
בְּחֵן בְּחֶֽסֶד וּבְרַחֲמִים
הוּא נוֹתֵן לֶֽחֶם לְכָל בָּשָׂר
כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ.
וּבְטוּבוֹ הַגָּדוֹל, תָּמִיד לֹא חָסַר לָֽנוּ
וְאַל יֶחְסַר לָֽנוּ מָזוֹן לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד
בַּעֲבוּר שְׁמוֹ הַגָּדוֹל.
כִּי הוּא אֵל זָן וּמְפַרְנֵס לַכֹּל
וּמֵטִיב לַכֹּל
וּמֵכִין מָזוֹן לְכָל בְּרִיּוֹתָיו אֲשֶׁר בָּרָא.
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה, הַזָּן אֶת הַכֹּל.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:26
segments.html: ברכת הארץ

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:27
segments.html:
נוֹדֶה לְךָ, יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ
עַל שֶׁהִנְחַֽלְתָּ לַאֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ אֶֽרֶץ חֶמְדָּה טוֹבָה וּרְחָבָה
וְעַל שֶׁהוֹצֵאתָֽנוּ יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֵאֶֽרֶץ מִצְרַֽיִם
וּפְדִיתָֽנוּ מִבֵּית עֲבָדִים
וְעַל בְּרִיתְךָ שֶׁחָתַֽמְתָּ בִּבְשָׂרֵֽנוּ
וְעַל תּוֹרָתְךָ שֶׁלִּמַּדְתָּֽנוּ
וְעַל חֻקֶּֽיךָ שֶׁהוֹדַעְתָּֽנוּ
וְעַל חַיִּים חֵן וָחֶֽסֶד שֶׁחוֹנַנְתָּֽנוּ
וְעַל אֲכִילַת מָזוֹן שָׁאַתָּה זָן וּמְפַרְנֵס אוֹתָֽנוּ תָּמִיד
בְּכָל יוֹם וּבְכָל עֵת וּבְכָל שָׁעָה.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:28
segments.html:
בחנוכה: עַל הַנִּסִּים וְעַל הַפֻּרְקָן וְעַל הַגְּבוּרוֹת וְעַל הַתְּשׁוּעוֹת וְעַל הַמִּלְחָמוֹת שֶׁעָשִֽׂיתָ לַאֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה.
בִּימֵי מַתִּתְיָֽהוּ בֶּן יוֹחָנָן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל חַשְׁמוֹנַאי וּבָנָיו, כְּשֶׁעָמְדָה מַלְכוּת יָוָן הָרְשָׁעָה עַל עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַשְׁכִּיחָם תּוֹרָתֶֽךָ וּלְהַעֲבִירָם מֵחֻקֵּי רְצוֹנֶֽךָ, וְאַתָּה בְּרַחֲמֶֽיךָ הָרַבִּים עָמַֽדְתָּ לָהֶם בְּעֵת צָרָתָם, רַֽבְתָּ אֶת רִיבָם, דַּֽנְתָּ אֶת דִּינָם, נָקַֽמְתָּ אֶת נִקְמָתָם, מָסַֽרְתָּ גִּבּוֹרִים בְּיַד חַלָּשִׁים, וְרַבִּים בְּיַד מְעַטִּים, וּטְמֵאִים בְּיַד טְהוֹרִים, וּרְשָׁעִים בְּיַד צַדִּיקִים, וְזֵדִים בְּיַד עוֹסְקֵי תוֹרָתֶֽךָ, וּלְךָ עָשִֽׂיתָ שֵׁם גָּדוֹל וְקָדוֹשׁ בְּעוֹלָמֶֽךָ, וּלְעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל עָשִֽׂיתָ תְּשׁוּעָה גְדוֹלָה וּפֻרְקָן כְּהַיּוֹם הַזֶּה. וְאַחַר כֵּן בָּֽאוּ בָנֶֽיךָ לִדְבִיר בֵּיתֶֽךָ, וּפִנּוּ אֶת הֵיכָלֶֽךָ, וְטִהֲרוּ אֶת מִקְדָּשֶֽׁךָ, וְהִדְלִֽיקוּ נֵרוֹת בְּחַצְרוֹת קָדְשֶֽׁךָ, וְקָבְעוּ שְׁמוֹנַת יְמֵי חֲנֻכָּה אֵֽלּוּ, לְהוֹדוֹת וּלְהַלֵּל לְשִׁמְךָ הַגָּדוֹל.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:29
segments.html:
בפורים: עַל הַנִּסִּים וְעַל הַפֻּרְקָן וְעַל הַגְּבוּרוֹת וְעַל הַתְּשׁוּעוֹת וְעַל הַמִּלְחָמוֹת שֶׁעָשִֽׂיתָ לַאֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה.
בִּימֵי מָרְדְּכַי וְאֶסְתֵּר בְּשׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה, כְּשֶׁעָמַד עֲלֵיהֶם הָמָן הָרָשָׁע, בִּקֵּשׁ לְהַשְׁמִיד לַהֲרֹג וּלְאַבֵּד אֶת־כָּל־הַיְּהוּדִים מִנַּֽעַר וְעַד־זָקֵן טַף וְנָשִׁים בְּיוֹם אֶחָד, בִּשְׁלוֹשָׁה עָשָׂר לְחֹֽדֶשׁ שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂר, הוּא־חֹֽדֶשׁ אֲדָר, וּשְׁלָלָם לָבוֹז: וְאַתָּה בְּרַחֲמֶֽיךָ הָרַבִּים הֵפַֽרְתָּ אֶת עֲצָתוֹ, וְקִלְקַֽלְתָּ אֶת מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ, וַהֲשֵׁבֽוֹתָ לּוֹ גְּמוּלוֹ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ, וְתָלוּ אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בָּנָיו עַל הָעֵץ.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:30
segments.html:
וְעַל הַכֹּל, יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ
אֲנַֽחְנוּ מוֹדִים לָךְ וּמְבָרְכִים אוֹתָךְ
יִתְבָּרַךְ שִׁמְךָ בְּפִי כָּל חַי תָּמִיד לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד
כַּכָּתוּב: וְאָכַלְתָּ וְשָׂבָֽעְתָּ, וּבֵרַכְתָּ אֶת־יהוה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ
עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ הַטֹּבָה אֲשֶׁר נָתַן־לָךְ׃
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה, עַל הָאָֽרֶץ וְעַל הַמָּזוֹן.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:31
segments.html: ברכת ירושלים

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:32
segments.html:
רַחֶם נָא, יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ
עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַמֶּֽךָ
וְעַל יְרוּשָׁלַֽיִם עִירֶֽךָ
וְעַל צִיּוֹן מִשְׁכַּן כְּבוֹדֶֽךָ
וְעַל מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד מְשִׁיחֶֽךָ
וְעַל הַבַּֽיִת הַגָּדוֹל וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁנִּקְרָא שִׁמְךָ עָלָיו.
אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ, אָבִֽינוּ
רְעֵֽנוּ, זוּנֵֽנוּ, פַּרְנְסֵֽנוּ וְכַלְכְּלֵֽנוּ
וְהַרְוִיחֵֽנוּ, וְהַרְוַח לָֽנוּ יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מְהֵרָה מִכָּל צָרוֹתֵֽינוּ.
וְנָא אַל תַּצְרִיכֵֽנוּ, יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ
לֹא לִידֵי מַתְּנַת בָּשָׂר וָדָם
וְלֹא לִידֵי הַלְוָאָתָם
כִּי אִם לְיָדְךָ הַמְּלֵאָה, הַפְּתוּחָה, הַקְּדוֹשָׁה וְהָרְחָבָה
שֶׁלֹּא נֵבוֹשׁ וְלֹא נִכָּלֵם לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:34
segments.html:
רְצֵה וְהַחֲלִיצֵֽנוּ, יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ, בְּמִצְוֹתֶֽיךָ
וּבְמִצְוַת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי הַשַּׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ הַזֶּה
כִּי יוֹם זֶה גָּדוֹל וְקָדוֹשׁ הוּא לְפָנֶֽיךָ
לִשְׁבָּת בּוֹ, וְלָנֽוּחַ בּוֹ בְּאַהֲבָה כְּמִצְוַת רְצוֹנֶֽךָ
וּבִרְצוֹנְךָ הָנִֽיחַ לָֽנוּ, יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ
שֶׁלֹּא תְהֵא צָרָה וְיָגוֹן וַאֲנָחָה בְּיוֹם מְנוּחָתֵֽנוּ
וְהַרְאֵֽנוּ, יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ, בְּנֶחָמַת צִיּוֹן עִירֶֽךָ
וּבְבִנְיַן יְרוּשָׁלַֽיִם עִיר קָדְשֶֽׁךָ
כִּי אַתָּה הוּא בַּֽעַל הַיְשׁוּעוֹת וּבַֽעַל הַנֶּחָמוֹת.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:36
segments.html:
אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ
יַעֲלֶה וְיָבוֹא וְיַגִּֽיעַ, וְיֵרָאֶה וְיֵרָצֶה וְיִשָּׁמַע
וְיִפָּקֵד וְיִזָּכֵר זִכְרוֹנֵֽנוּ וּפִקְדוֹנֵֽנוּ, וְזִכְרוֹן אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ
וְזִכְרוֹן מָשִֽׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד עַבְדֶּֽךָ
וְזִכְרוֹן יְרוּשָׁלַֽיִם עִיר קָדְשֶֽׁךָ
וְזִכְרוֹן כָּל עַמְּךָ בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל
לְפָנֶֽיךָ, לִפְלֵיטָה לְטוֹבָה, לְחֵן וּלְחֶֽסֶד וּלְרַחֲמִים
לְחַיִּים וּלְשָׁלוֹם בְּיוֹם
בראש חודש: רֹאשׁ הַחֹֽדֶשׁ הַזֶּה.
בראש השנה: הַזִּכָּרוֹן הַזֶּה.
בפסח: חַג הַמַּצּוֹת הַזֶּה.
בשבועות: חַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת הַזֶּה.
בסוכות: חַג הַסֻּכּוֹת הַזֶּה.
בשמיני עצרת ושמחת תורה: הַשְּׁמִינִי חַג הָעֲצֶֽרֶת הַזֶּה.
זָכְרֵֽנוּ יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ בּוֹ לְטוֹבָה
וּפָקְדֵֽנוּ בוֹ לִבְרָכָה
וְהוֹשִׁיעֵֽנוּ בוֹ לְחַיִּים.
וּבִדְבַר יְשׁוּעָה וְרַחֲמִים, חוּס וְחָנֵּֽנוּ וְרַחֵם עָלֵֽינוּ, וְהוֹשִׁיעֵֽנוּ
כִּי אֵלֶֽיךָ עֵינֵֽינוּ, כִּי אֵל (מֶֽלֶךְ) חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם אָֽתָּה.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:38
segments.html:
וּבְנֵה יְרוּשָׁלַֽיִם עִיר הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵֽינוּ.
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה, בּוֹנֶה בְרַחֲמָיו יְרוּשָׁלָֽיִם, אָמֵן.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:39
segments.html: ברכת הטוב והמטיב

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:40
segments.html:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם
הָאֵל אָבִֽינוּ, מַלְכֵּֽנוּ, אַדִּירֵֽנוּ
בּוֹרְאֵֽנוּ, גּוֹאֲלֵֽנוּ, יוֹצְרֵֽנוּ, קְדוֹשֵֽׁנוּ, קְדוֹשׁ יַעֲקֹב
רוֹעֵֽנוּ, רוֹעֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל, הַמֶּֽלֶךְ הַטּוֹב וְהַמֵּיטִיב לַכֹּל, שֶׁבְּכָל יוֹם וָיוֹם
הוּא הֵיטִיב, הוּא מֵיטִיב, הוּא יֵיטִיב לָֽנוּ
הוּא גְמָלָֽנוּ, הוּא גוֹמְלֵֽנוּ, הוּא יִגְמְלֵֽנוּ לָעַד
לְחֵן וּלְחֶֽסֶד וּלְרַחֲמִים, וּלְרֶֽוַח, הַצָּלָה וְהַצְלָחָה
בְּרָכָה וִישׁוּעָה, נֶחָמָה, פַּרְנָסָה וְכַלְכָּלָה
וְרַחֲמִים וְחַיִּים וְשָׁלוֹם וְכָל טוֹב, וּמִכָּל טוּב לְעוֹלָם אַל יְחַסְּרֵֽנוּ.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:42
segments.html: הָרַחֲמָן הוּא יִמְלֹךְ עָלֵֽינוּ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:43
segments.html: הָרַחֲמָן הוּא יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּשָּׁמַֽיִם וּבָאָֽרֶץ.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:44
segments.html:
הָרַחֲמָן הוּא יִשְׁתַּבַּח לְדוֹר דּוֹרִים, וְיִתְפָּאַר בָּֽנוּ לָעַד וּלְנֵֽצַח נְצָחִים
וְיִתְהַדַּר בָּֽנוּ לָעַד וּלְעוֹלְמֵי עוֹלָמִים.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:45
segments.html: הָרַחֲמָן הוּא יְפַרְנְסֵֽנוּ בְּכָבוֹד.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:46
segments.html:
הָרַחֲמָן הוּא יִשְׁבֹּר עֻלֵּֽנוּ מֵעַל צַוָּארֵֽנוּ
וְהוּא יוֹלִיכֵֽנוּ קוֹמְמִיּוּת לְאַרְצֵֽנוּ.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:47
segments.html:
הָרַחֲמָן הוּא יִשְׁלַח לָֽנוּ בְּרָכָה מְרֻבָּה בַּבַּֽיִת הַזֶּה
וְעַל שֻׁלְחָן זֶה שֶׁאָכַֽלְנוּ עָלָיו.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:48
segments.html:
הָרַחֲמָן הוּא יִשְׁלַח לָֽנוּ אֶת אֵלִיָּֽהוּ הַנָּבִיא זָכוּר לַטּוֹב
וִיבַשֶּׂר לָֽנוּ בְּשׂוֹרוֹת טוֹבוֹת יְשׁוּעוֹת וְנֶחָמוֹת.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:49
segments.html: הָרַחֲמָן הוּא יְבָרֵךְ אֶת מְדִינַת יִשְׂרָאֵל, רֵאשִׁית צְמִיחַת גְּאֻלָּתֵֽנוּ.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:50
segments.html:
הָרַחֲמָן הוּא יְבָרֵךְ אֶת חַיָּלֵי צְבָא הַהֲגָנָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
הָעוֹמְדִים עַל מִשְׁמַר אַרְצֵֽנוּ.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:52

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:4
segments.html: Blessed are You, <small>LORD</small> our God, King of the Universe, who brings forth bread from the earth.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:5
segments.html: <small>BIRKAT HAMAZON / GRACE AFTER MEALS</small>

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:6
segments.html: On days when Taḥanun is said:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:7
segments.html: עַל־נַהֲרוֹת By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept as we remembered Zion. There on the willow trees we hung up our harps, for there our captors asked us for songs, our tormentors, for amusement, said: “Sing us one of the songs of Zion!” How can we sing the <small>LORD</small>’s song on foreign soil? If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand forget its skill. May my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you, if I do not set Jerusalem above my highest joy. Remember, <small>LORD</small>, what the Edomites did on the day Jerusalem fell. They said, “Tear it down, tear it down to its very foundations!” Daughter of Babylon, doomed to destruction, happy is he who repays you for what you have done to us, who seizes your infants and dashes them against the rocks.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:8
segments.html: On days when Taḥanun is omitted (such as Shabbat and Yom Tov, see full list on page 144 ):

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:9
segments.html: שִׁיר הַמַּעֲלוֹת A song of ascents. When the <small>LORD</small> brought back the exiles of Zion we were like people who dream. Then were our mouths filled with laughter, and our tongues with songs of joy. Then was it said among the nations, “The <small>LORD</small> has done great things for them.” The <small>LORD</small> did do great things for us and we rejoiced. Bring back our exiles, <small>LORD</small>, like streams in a dry land. May those who sowed in tears, reap in joy. May one who goes out weeping, carrying a bag of seed, come back with songs of joy, carrying his sheaves.

segments.html:
תְּהִלַּת My mouth shall speak the praise of God, and all creatures shall bless His holy name for ever and all time. We will bless God now and for ever.
Halleluya! Thank the LORD for He is good; His loving-kindness is for ever. Who can tell of the LORD’s mighty acts and make all His praise be heard?

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:12
segments.html: <small>ZIMMUN / INVITATION</small>

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:13
segments.html:
For the zimmun said at a wedding or during the week of Sheva Berakhot, see page 1042. At a Brit, see page 1020. In the house of a mourner when there are three or more men, see page 1068.
When three or more men say Birkat HaMazon together, the following zimmun is said.
When three or more women say Birkat HaMazon, substitute “Friends” for “Gentlemen.”
The leader should ask permission from those with precedence to lead the Birkat HaMazon.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:14
segments.html: Leader Gentlemen, let us say grace.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:15
segments.html: Others May the name of the LORD be blessed from now and for ever.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:16
segments.html: Leader May the name of the LORD be blessed from now and for ever.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:17
segments.html: With your permission, (my father and teacher / my mother and teacher / the Kohanim present / our teacher the Rabbi / the master of this house / the mistress of this house)

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:18
segments.html:
my masters and teachers,
let us bless (in a minyan our God,) the One from whose food we have eaten.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:19
segments.html: Others Blessed be (in a minyan: our God,) the One from whose food we have eaten, and by whose goodness we live.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:20
segments.html: * People present who have not taken part in the meal say:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:21
segments.html: *Blessed be (in a minyan: our God,) the One whose name is continually blessed for ever and all time.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:22
segments.html: Leader Blessed be (in a minyan: our God,) the One from whose food we have eaten, and by whose goodness we live.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:23
segments.html: Blessed be He, and blessed be His name.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:24
segments.html: <small>BLESSING OF NOURISHMENT</small>

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:25
segments.html:
בָּרוּךְ Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who in His goodness feeds the whole world
with grace, kindness and compassion.
He gives food to all living things,
for His kindness is for ever.
Because of His continual great goodness,
we have never lacked food,
nor may we ever lack it, for the sake of His great name.
For He is God who feeds and sustains all,
does good to all,
and prepares food for all creatures He has created.
Blessed are You, LORD, who feeds all.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:26
segments.html: <small>BLESSING OF LAND</small>

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:27
segments.html:
נוֹדֶה We thank You, LORD our God,
for having granted as a heritage to our ancestors
a desirable, good and spacious land;
for bringing us out, LORD our God, from the land of Egypt,
freeing us from the house of slavery;
for Your covenant which You sealed in our flesh;
for Your Torah which You taught us;
for Your laws which You made known to us;
for the life, grace and kindness You have bestowed on us;
and for the food by which You continually feed and sustain us,
every day, every season, every hour.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:28
segments.html:
On Ḥanukka: עַל הַנִּסִּים [We thank You also] for the miracles, the redemption, the mighty deeds, the salvations, and the victories in battle which You performed for our ancestors in those days, at this time
.בִּימֵי מַתִּתְיָֽהוּ In the days of Mattityahu, son of Yoḥanan, the High Priest, the Hasmonean, and his sons, the wicked Greek kingdom rose up against Your people Israel to make them forget Your Torah and to force them to transgress the statutes of Your will. It was then that You in Your great compassion stood by them in the time of their distress. You championed their cause, judged their claim, and avenged their wrong. You delivered the strong into the hands of the weak, the many into the hands of the few, the impure into the hands of the pure, the wicked into the hands of the righteous, and the arrogant into the hands of those who were engaged in the study of Your Torah. You made for Yourself great and holy renown in Your world, and for Your people Israel You performed a great salvation and redemption as of this very day. Your children then entered the holiest part of Your House, cleansed Your Temple, purified Your Sanctuary, kindled lights in Your holy courts, and designated these eight days of Ḥanukka for giving thanks and praise to Your great name.
Continue with “For all this.”

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:29
segments.html:
On Purim: עַל הַנִּסִּים [We thank You also] for the miracles, the redemption, the mighty deeds, the salvations, and the victories in battle which You performed for our ancestors in those days, at this time
.בִּימֵי מָרְדְּכַי In the days of Mordekhai and Esther, in Shushan the capital, the wicked Haman rose up against them and sought to destroy, slay and exterminate all the Jews, young and old, children and women, on one day, the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar, and to plunder their possessions. Then You in Your great compassion thwarted his counsel, frustrated his plans, and caused his scheme to recoil on his own head, so that they hanged him and his sons on the gallows.
Continue with “For all this.”

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:30
segments.html:
וְעַל הַכֹּל For all this, LORD our God, we thank and bless You.
May Your name be blessed continually
by the mouth of all that lives, for ever and all time –
for so it is written: “You will eat and be satisfied, then you shall bless the LORD your God for the good land He has given you.” Blessed are You, LORD, for the land and for the food.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:31
segments.html: <small>BLESSING FOR JERUSALEM</small>

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:32
segments.html:
רַחֶם נָא Have compassion, please, LORD our God,
on Israel Your people,
on Jerusalem Your city,
on Zion the dwelling place of Your glory,
on the royal house of David Your anointed,
and on the great and holy House that bears Your name.
Our God, our Father,
tend us, feed us,
sustain us and support us,
relieve us and send us relief, LORD our God, swiftly from all our troubles.
Please, LORD our God, do not make us dependent on the gifts or loans of other people,
but only on Your full, open, holy and generous hand
so that we may suffer neither shame nor humiliation for ever and all time.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:33
segments.html: On Shabbat, say:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:34
segments.html:
רְצֵה Favor and strengthen us, LORD our God, through Your commandments,
especially through the commandment of the seventh day, this great and holy Sabbath.
For it is, for You, a great and holy day.
On it we cease work and rest in love in accord with Your will’s commandment.
May it be Your will, LORD our God,
to grant us rest without distress, grief, or lament on our day of rest.
May You show us the consolation of Zion Your city,
and the rebuilding of Jerusalem Your holy city,
for You are the Master of salvation and consolation.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:35
segments.html: On Rosh Ḥodesh and Festivals, say:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:36
segments.html:
אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ Our God and God of our ancestors,
may there rise, come, reach, appear, be favored, heard, regarded
and remembered before You, our recollection and remembrance,
as well as the remembrance of our ancestors,
and of the Messiah son of David Your servant,
and of Jerusalem Your holy city,
and of all Your people the house of Israel –
for deliverance and well-being, grace, loving-kindness and compassion, life and peace, on this day of:
On Rosh Ḥodesh: Rosh Ḥodesh.
On Rosh HaShana: the Day of Memorial.
On Pesaḥ: the Festival of Matzot.
On Shavuot: the Festival of Shavuot.
On Sukkot: the Festival of Sukkot.
On Shemini Atzeret & Simḥat Torah: the Festival of Shemini Atzeret.
On it remember us, LORD our God, for good;
recollect us for blessing,
and deliver us for life.
In accord with Your promise of salvation and compassion,
spare us and be gracious to us;
have compassion on us and deliver us,
for our eyes are turned to You because You are God,
gracious and compassionate (King).

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:37
segments.html: In the house of a mourner, “Comfort” on page 1068 is substituted for the next two paragraphs.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:38
segments.html:
וּבְנֵה And may Jerusalem the holy city be rebuilt soon, in our time.
Blessed are You, LORD, who in His compassion
will rebuild Jerusalem. Amen.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:39
segments.html: <small>BLESSING OF GOD'S GOODNESS</small>

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:40
segments.html:
בָּרוּךְ Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe –
God our Father, our King, our Sovereign,
our Creator, our Redeemer, our Maker,
our Holy One, the Holy One of Jacob.
He is our Shepherd, Israel’s Shepherd,
the good King who does good to all.
Every day He has done, is doing, and will do good to us.
He has acted, is acting, and will always act kindly toward us for ever,
granting us grace, kindness and compassion, relief and rescue,
prosperity, blessing, redemption and comfort,
sustenance and support, compassion, life, peace and all good things,
and of all good things may He never let us lack.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:41
segments.html: <small>ADDITIONAL REQUESTS</small>

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:42
segments.html: הָרַחֲמָן May the Compassionate One reign over us for ever and all time.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:43
segments.html: May the Compassionate One be blessed in heaven and on earth.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:44
segments.html:
May the Compassionate One be praised from generation to generation, be glorified by us to all eternity,
and honored among us for ever and all time.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:45
segments.html: May the Compassionate One grant us an honorable livelihood.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:46
segments.html:
May the Compassionate One break the yoke from our neck
and lead us upright to our land.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:47
segments.html:
May the Compassionate One send us many blessings to this house
and this table at which we have eaten.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:48
segments.html:
May the Compassionate One send us Elijah the prophet –
may he be remembered for good –
to bring us good tidings of salvation and consolation.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:49
segments.html: May the Compassionate One bless the State of Israel, first flowering of our redemption.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:50
segments.html:
May the Compassionate One bless
the members of Israel’s Defense Forces,
who stand guard over our land.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:51
segments.html: A guest says:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:52
segments.html: יְהִי רָצוֹן May it be Your will that the master of this house shall not suffer shame in this world, nor humiliation in the World to Come. May all he owns prosper greatly, and may his and our possessions be successful and close to hand. Let not the Accuser hold sway over his deeds or ours, and may no thought of sin, iniquity or transgression enter him or us from now and for evermore.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:53
segments.html: הָרַחֲמָן May the Compassionate One bless –

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:54
segments.html: When eating at one’s own table, say (include the words in parentheses that apply):

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:55
segments.html:
me, (my wife/husband, / my father, my teacher / my mother,
my teacher/ my children,) and all that is mine,

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:56
segments.html: A guest at someone else’s table says (include the words in parentheses that apply):

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:57
segments.html:
the master of this house, him (and his wife,
the mistress of this house / and his children,) and all that is his,

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:58
segments.html: Children at their parents’ table say (include the words in parentheses that apply):

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:59
segments.html: my father, my teacher, (master of this house,) and my mother, my teacher, (mistress of this house,) them, their household, their children, and all that is theirs.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:60
segments.html: For all other guests, add:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:61
segments.html:
and all the diners here,
אוֹתָֽנוּ – together with us and all that is ours.
Just as our forefathers
Abraham, Isaac and Jacob were blessed in all, from all, with all,
so may He bless all of us together with a complete blessing,
and let us say: Amen.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:62
segments.html:
בַּמָּרוֹם On high, may grace be invoked for them and for us, as a safeguard of peace.
May we receive a blessing from the LORD
and a just reward from the God of our salvation,
and may we find grace and good favor in the eyes of God and man.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:63
segments.html: At a circumcision feast add here “May the Compassionate One bless the father” on page 1022.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:64
segments.html: On Shabbat: May the Compassionate One let us inherit the time, that will be entirely Shabbat and rest for life everlasting.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:65
segments.html:
On Rosh Ḥodesh: May the Compassionate One renew this month for us,
for good and blessing.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:66
segments.html: On Rosh HaShana: May the Compassionate One renew for us this year, for good and blessing.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:67
segments.html: On Yom Tov: May the Compassionate One let us inherit the day, that is all good.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:68
segments.html: On Sukkot: May the Compassionate One restore for us, the fallen Tabernacle of David.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:69
segments.html:
הָרַחֲמָן May the Compassionate One make us worthy of the Messianic Age and life in the World to Come.
He gives great /On Shabbat, Festivals, and Rosh Ḥodesh: He is a tower of / salvation to His king, showing kindness to His anointed, to David and his descendants for ever. He who makes peace in His high places, may He make peace for us and all Israel, and let us say: Amen.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:70
segments.html:
יְראוּ Fear the LORD, you His holy ones;
those who fear Him lack nothing.
Young lions may grow weak and hungry,
but those who seek the LORD lack no good thing.
Thank the LORD for He is good;
His loving-kindness is for ever.
You open Your hand,
and satisfy every living thing with favor.
Blessed is the person who trusts in the LORD,
whose trust is in the LORD alone.
Once I was young, and now I am old,
yet I have never watched a righteous man forsaken or his children begging for bread.
The LORD will give His people strength.
The LORD will bless His people with peace.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:71
segments.html: If Birkat HaMazon was made on a cup of wine, then the blessing over wine is made and the majority of the cup is drunk, after which Al HaMiḥya, page 994, is said.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:72
segments.html: At a wedding or Sheva Berakhot, turn to page 1040:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:73
segments.html: Before eating food, other than bread or matza, made from the five species of grain (wheat, barley, rye, oats and spelt), or rice:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:74
segments.html: Blessed are You, the <small>LORD</small> our God, King of the Universe, who creates the various kinds of nourishment.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:75
segments.html: Before drinking wine or grape juice:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:76
segments.html: Blessed are You, <small>LORD</small> our God, King of the Universe, who creates the fruit of the vine.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:77
segments.html: Before eating fruit that grows on trees:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:78
segments.html: Blessed are You, <small>LORD</small> our God, King of the Universe, who creates the fruit of the tree.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:79
segments.html: Before eating vegetables, or fruit that does not grow on trees:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:80
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who creates the fruit of the ground.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:81
segments.html: Before eating other food or drinking other liquids:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:82
segments.html: Blessed are You, <small>LORD</small> our God, King of the Universe, by whose word all things came to be.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:83
segments.html:
Before eating fruit for the first time in a season, the following is said.
This blessing is also said when buying or wearing a new garment of significant value (e.g. a dress or suit); entering a new home for the first time; or hearing personal good news.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:84
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who has given us life, sustained us, and brought us to this time.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:85
segments.html: <small>BLESSING AFTER FOOD -- AL HAMIḤYA</small>

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:86
segments.html: Grace after eating from the “seven species” of produce with which Israel is blessed: food made from the five grains (but not bread); wine or grape juice; grapes, figs, pomegranates, olives, or dates.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:87
segments.html: בָּרוּךְ Blessed are You, <small>LORD</small> our God, King of the Universe,

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:88
segments.html:
After grain products (but not bread or matza): for the nourishment and sustenance,
After wine or grape juice: for the vine and the fruit of the vine,
After grapes, figs, olives, pomegranates or dates: for the tree and the fruit of the tree,
After grain products (but not bread or matza), and wine or grape juice: for the nourishment and sustenance and for the vine and the fruit of the vine,

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:89
segments.html: and for the produce of the field; for the desirable, good and spacious land that You willingly gave as heritage to our ancestors, that they might eat of its fruit and be satisfied with its goodness. Have compassion, please, <small>LORD</small> our God, on Israel Your people, on Jerusalem, Your city, on Zion the home of Your glory, on Your altar and Your Temple. May You rebuild Jerusalem, the holy city swiftly in our time, and may You bring us back there, rejoicing in its rebuilding, eating from its fruit, satisfied by its goodness, and blessing You for it in holiness and purity.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:90
segments.html:
On Shabbat: Be pleased to refresh us on this Sabbath Day.
On Rosh Ḥodesh: Remember us for good on this day of the New Moon.
On Rosh HaShana: Remember us for good on this Day of Remembrance.
On Pesaḥ: Grant us joy on this Festival of Matzot.
On Shavuot: Grant us joy on this Festival of Shavuot.
On Sukkot: Grant us joy on this Festival of Sukkot.
On Shemini Atzeret & Simḥat Torah: Grant us joy on this Festival of Shemini Atzeret.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:91
segments.html:
For You, LORD, are good and do good to all and we thank You for the land
After grain products (but not bread or matza): and for the nourishment. Blessed are You, Lord, for the land and for the nourishment.
After wine or grape juice: and for the fruit of the vine.* Blessed are You, Lord, for the land and for the fruit of the vine.*
After grapes, figs, olives, pomegranates or dates: and for the fruit.** Blessed are You, Lord, for the land and for the fruit.**
After grain products (but not bread or matza), and wine or grape juice: and for the nourishment and for the fruit of the vine.*
Blessed are You, Lord, for the land and for the nourishment and the fruit of the vine.*

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:92
segments.html:
* If the wine is from Israel, then substitute “her vine” for “the vine.”
** If the fruit is from Israel, then substitute “her fruit” for “the fruit.”

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:93
segments.html: <small>BLESSING AFTER FOOD – BOREH NEFASHOT</small>

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:94
segments.html: After food or drink that does not require Birkat HaMazon or Al HaMiḥya – such as meat, fish, dairy products, vegetables, beverages, or fruit other than grapes, figs, pomegranates, olives or dates – say:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Birkat HaMazon; Grace after Meals:95
segments.html: בָּרוּךְ Blessed are You, <small>LORD</small> our God, King of the Universe, who creates the many forms of life and their needs. For all You have created to sustain the life of all that lives, blessed be He, Giver of life to the worlds.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:2
segments.html:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָֽׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו
וְצִוָּֽנוּ לְהַפְרִישׁ תְּרוּמוֹת וּמַעְשְׂרוֹת.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:3

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:1
segments.html: In Israel on separating teruma and first tithe (if there is doubt as to whether the teruma and first tithe have been taken, the following blessing is not said, but the subsequent declaration is):

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:2
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe, who has made us holy through His commandments,
and has commanded us to separate terumot and tithes.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:3
segments.html: Whatever [of the allocated portion] is more than one in a hundred of everything here, is hereby declared to be teruma gedola [the priestly portion] and is the northern portion. The one in a hundred that remains here, together with nine equal portions on the upper side of this produce are declared to be the first [levitical] tithe. The one in a hundred I have made first tithe is hereby declared to be terumat ma’aser [the tithe-of-the-tithe set aside for the priests]. Nine other equal portions on the lower side of the produce are declared to be second tithe, but if this produce must have the tithe of the poor separated from it, let them be the tithe of the poor.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:4
segments.html: In Israel on separating and redeeming the second tithe (if there is doubt as to whether the second tithe has been taken, the following blessing is not said, but the subsequent declaration is):

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:5
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe, who has made us holy through His commandments,
and has commanded us about the redemption of the second tithe.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:6
segments.html: This second tithe, together with its additional fifth, is hereby redeemed by one peruta of the coins I have set aside for the redemption of the second tithe.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:7
segments.html: On taking ḥalla:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:8
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe, who has made us holy through His commandments,
and has commanded us to set aside ḥalla from the dough.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:9
segments.html: On redeeming fourth-year fruit:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:10
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe, who has made us holy through His commandments,
and has commanded us about the redemption of fruit of the fourth year.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:11
segments.html: On fixing a mezuza to the doorpost:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:12
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe, who has made us holy through His commandments,
and has commanded us to affix the mezuza.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:13
segments.html: On making a protective railing around one’s roof, or a fence around a pit:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:14
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe, who has made us holy through His commandments,
and has commanded us to to affix a guard-rail.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:15
segments.html: A woman on ritual immersion:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:16
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe, who has made us holy through His commandments,
and has commanded us about ritual immersion.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:17
segments.html: On immersing utensils made by or bought from a gentile:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Mitzvot:18
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe, who has made us holy through His commandments,

segments.html: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, אֲשֶׁר יָצַר אֶתְכֶם בַּדִּין, וְזָן וְכִלְכֵּל אֶתְכֶם בַּדִּין, וְהֵמִית אֶתְכֶם בַּדִּין, וְיוֹדֵֽעַ מִסְפַּר כֻּלְּכֶם בַּדִּין, וְהוּא עָתִיד לְהַחֲיוֹתְכֶם וּלְקַיֵּם אֶתְכֶם בַּדִּין. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה, מְחַיֵּה הַמֵּתִים.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:50
segments.html: אַתָּה גִּבּוֹר לְעוֹלָם אֲדֹנָי, מְחַיֵּה מֵתִים אַתָּה, רַב לְהוֹשִֽׁיעַ, מְכַלְכֵּל חַיִּים בְּחֶֽסֶד, מְחַיֵּה מֵתִים בְּרַחֲמִים רַבִּים, סוֹמֵךְ נוֹפְלִים, וְרוֹפֵא חוֹלִים, וּמַתִּיר אֲסוּרִים, וּמְקַיֵּם אֱמוּנָתוֹ לִישֵׁנֵי עָפָר. מִי כָמֽוֹךָ בַּֽעַל גְּבוּרוֹת וּמִי דּֽוֹמֶה לָּךְ, מֶֽלֶךְ מֵמִית וּמְחַיֶּה וּמַצְמִֽיחַ יְשׁוּעָה, וְנֶאֱמָן אַתָּה לְהַחֲיוֹת מֵתִים.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:52
segments.html: הֲבִינֵֽנוּ יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ לָדַֽעַת דְּרָכֶֽיךָ, וּמוֹל אֶת לְבָבֵֽנוּ לְיִרְאָתֶֽךָ, וְתִסְלַח לָֽנוּ לִהְיוֹת גְּאוּלִים, וְרַחֲקֵֽנוּ מִמַּכְאוֹב, וְדַשְּׁנֵֽנוּ בִּנְאוֹת אַרְצֶֽךָ, וּנְפוּצוֹתֵֽינוּ מֵאַרְבַּע תְּקַבֵּֽץ, וְהַתּוֹעִים עַל דַּעְתְּךָ יִשָּׁפֵֽטוּ, וְעַל הָרְשָׁעִים תָּנִיף יָדֶֽךָ, וְיִשְׂמְחוּ צַדִּיקִים בְּבִנְיַן עִירֶֽךָ וּבְתִקּוּן הֵיכָלֶֽךָ, וּבִצְמִיחַת קֶרֶן לְדָוִד עַבְדֶּֽךָ וּבַעֲרִיכַת נֵר לְבֶן יִשַׁי מְשִׁיחֶֽךָ, טֶֽרֶם נִקְרָא אַתָּה תַעֲנֶה. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה, שׁוֹמֵֽע תְּפִלָּה.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:54
segments.html: צָרְכֵי עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל מְרֻבִּים וְדַעְתָּם קְצָרָה. יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶֽיךָ יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ, שֶׁתִּתֵּן לְכָל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד כְּדֵי פַּרְנָסָתוֹ, וּלְכָל גְּוִיָּה וּגְוִיָּה דֵּי מַחְסוֹרָהּ, וְהַטּוֹב בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ עֲשֵׂה. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה, שׁוֹמֵֽעַ תְּפִלָּה.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:1
segments.html: On wearing new clothes:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:2
segments.html: Blessed are You, <small>LORD</small> our God, King of the Universe, who clothes the naked.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:3
segments.html: On smelling fragrant shrubs or trees:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:4
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who creates fragrant trees.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:5
segments.html: On smelling fragrant herbs, grasses or flowers:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:6
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who creates fragrant plants.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:7
segments.html: On smelling fragrant fruit:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:8
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who gives pleasant fragrance to fruits.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:9
segments.html: On smelling persimmon oil:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:10
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who creates pleasing perfume.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:11
segments.html: On all other scents:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:12
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who creates the various spices.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:13
segments.html: On seeing the wonders of nature, such as lightning, and on the 28-year solar cycle:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:14
segments.html: Blessed are You, <small>LORD</small> our God, King of the Universe, Author of creation.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:15
segments.html: On hearing thunder or experiencing a hurricane:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:16
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
whose power and might fill the world.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:17
segments.html: On seeing a rainbow:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:18
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who remembers the covenant, is faithful to the covenant, and fulfills His word.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:19
segments.html: On seeing the ocean or the Mediterranean Sea for the first time in thirty days:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:20
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who has made the great sea.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:21
segments.html: On seeing trees blossoming for the first time in the year:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:22
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who has withheld nothing from His world,
but has created in it beautiful creatures and trees for human beings to enjoy.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:23
segments.html: On seeing beautiful scenes of nature:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:24
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who has [created] such things in His world.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:25
segments.html: On seeing unusual people or animals:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:26
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who makes [all] creatures different.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:27
segments.html: On hearing good news from which others as well as oneself will benefit:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:28
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who is good and does good.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:29
segments.html: On hearing bad news, and said by a mourner before the ritual tearing of the garment:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:30
segments.html: Blessed are You, <small>LORD</small> our God, King of the Universe, the true Judge.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:31
segments.html: On seeing an outstanding Torah scholar:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:32
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who has shared of His wisdom with those who revere Him.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:33
segments.html: On seeing an outstanding secular scholar:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:34
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who has given of His wisdom to human beings.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:35
segments.html: On seeing a Monarch or Head of State:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:36
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who has given of His glory to human beings.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:37
segments.html: On seeing 600,000 Jews together in Israel:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:38
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who knows all secrets.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:39
segments.html: On seeing Jewish settlements in Israel:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:40
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who establishes the border of the widow.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:41
segments.html: On seeing the place where miracles occurred to the Jewish people:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:42
segments.html:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the Universe,
who performed miracles for our ancestors in this place.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:43
segments.html: On seeing the place where miracles occurred to oneself or one’s family (insert the relevant words):

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:44
segments.html: Blessed are You, <small>LORD</small> our God, King of the Universe, who performed a miracle for me (my father / my mother / my ancestors) in this place.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:45
segments.html: <small>ADDITIONAL BLESSINGS</small>

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:46
segments.html: After relieving oneself and washing one’s hands, say:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:47
segments.html: Blessed are You, <small>LORD</small> our God, King of the Universe, who formed man in wisdom and created in him many orifices and cavities. It is revealed and known before the throne of Your glory that were one of them to be ruptured or blocked, it would be impossible to survive and stand before You. Blessed are You, <small>LORD</small>, Healer of all flesh who does wondrous deeds.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:48
segments.html: On visiting a cemetery, or seeing a Jewish grave, for the first time in thirty days:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:49
segments.html: Blessed are You, <small>LORD</small> our God, King of the Universe, who formed you in judgment, who nourished and sustained you in judgment, who brought death on you in judgment, who knows the number of you all in judgment, and who in the future will restore you to life in judgment. Blessed are You, <small>LORD</small>, who revives the dead.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:50
segments.html: You are eternally mighty, <small>LORD</small>. You give life to the dead and have great power to save. He sustains the living with loving-kindness, and with great compassion revives the dead. He supports the fallen, heals the sick, sets captives free, and keeps His faith with those who sleep in the dust. Who is like You, Master of might, and who can compare to You, O King who brings death and gives life, and makes salvation grow? Faithful are You to revive the dead.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:51
segments.html: In special cases of urgency only (see law 363), the following short form of the Amida may be said. First say the first three blessings of the Amida from “O LORD” on page 108 until “the holy God” page 114, then say:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:52
segments.html: הֲבִינֵֽנוּ Grant us understanding, <small>LORD</small> our God, to know Your ways. Sensitize our hearts so that we may revere You, and forgive us so that we may be redeemed. Keep us far from suffering and satisfy us with the pastures of Your land. Gather our scattered people from the four quarters of the earth. May those who go astray be judged according to Your will: raise Your hand against the wicked. May the righteous rejoice in the rebuilding of Your city, the restoration of Your Temple, the flowering of Your servant David’s glory, and the radiant light of the son of Jesse, Your anointed. May You answer us even before we call. Blessed are You, <small>LORD</small>, who hears prayer.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:53
segments.html: In extreme cases where there is no time to say the abbreviated Amida above, one may say the following. However, if prayer is then possible at a later time, one should say the complete Amida.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Blessings on Pleasures, Sights and Sounds:54
segments.html: צָרְכֵי The needs of Your people Israel are many, and their patience is thin. May it be Your will, <small>LORD</small> our God and God of our ancestors, to give each one of them enough to sustain him, and to every single body, all that it lacks – and perform what is right in Your eyes. Blessed are You, <small>LORD</small>, who listens to prayer.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Consecration of a House:1
segments.html: מִזְמוֹר שִׁיר־חֲנֻכַּת הַבַּֽיִת לְדָוִד׃ אֲרוֹמִמְךָ יהוה כִּי דִלִּיתָֽנִי, וְלֹא־שִׂמַּֽחְתָּ אֹיְבַי לִי׃ יהוה אֱלֹהָי, שִׁוַּֽעְתִּי אֵלֶֽיךָ וַתִּרְפָּאֵֽנִי׃ יהוה, הֶעֱלִֽיתָ מִן־שְׁאוֹל נַפְשִׁי, חִיִּיתַֽנִי מִיָּרְדִי־בוֹר׃ זַמְּרוּ לַיהוה חֲסִידָיו, וְהוֹדוּ לְזֵֽכֶר קָדְשׁוֹ׃ כִּי רֶֽגַע בְּאַפּוֹ, חַיִּים בִּרְצוֹנוֹ, בָּעֶֽרֶב יָלִין בֶּֽכִי וְלַבֹּֽקֶר רִנָּה׃ וַאֲנִי אָמַֽרְתִּי בְשַׁלְוִי, בַּל־אֶמּוֹט לְעוֹלָם׃ יהוה, בִּרְצוֹנְךָ הֶעֱמַֽדְתָּה לְהַרְרִי עֹז, הִסְתַּֽרְתָּ פָנֶֽיךָ הָיִֽיתִי נִבְהָל׃ אֵלֶֽיךָ יהוה אֶקְרָא, וְאֶל־אֲדֹנָי אֶתְחַנָּן׃ מַה־בֶּֽצַע בְּדָמִי, בְּרִדְתִּי אֶל שָֽׁחַת, הֲיוֹדְךָ עָפָר, הֲיַגִּיד אֲמִתֶּֽךָ׃ שְׁמַע־יהוה וְחָנֵּֽנִי, יהוה הֱיֵה־עֹזֵר לִי׃ הָפַֽכְתָּ מִסְפְּדִי לְמָחוֹל לִי, פִּתַּֽחְתָּ שַׂקִּי, וַתְּאַזְּרֵֽנִי שִׂמְחָה׃ לְמַֽעַן יְזַמֶּרְךָ כָבוֹד וְלֹא יִדֹּם, יהוה אֱלֹהַי, לְעוֹלָם אוֹדֶֽךָּ׃

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Consecration of a House:2
segments.html: מִזְמוֹר לְדָוִד, יהוה מִי־יָגוּר בְּאָהֳלֶֽךָ, מִי־יִשְׁכֹּן בְּהַר קָדְשֶֽׁךָ׃ הוֹלֵךְ תָּמִים וּפֹעֵל צֶֽדֶק, וְדֹבֵר אֱמֶת בִּלְבָבוֹ׃ לֹא־רָגַל עַל־לְשֹׁנוֹ, לֹא־עָשָׂה לְרֵעֵֽהוּ רָעָה, וְחֶרְפָּה לֹא־נָשָׂא עַל־קְרֹבוֹ׃ נִבְזֶה בְּעֵינָיו נִמְאָס, וְאֶת־יִרְאֵי יהוה יְכַבֵּד, נִשְׁבַּע לְהָרַע וְלֹא יָמִר׃ כַּסְפּוֹ לֹא־נָתַן בְּנֶֽשֶׁךְ, וְשֹֽׁחַד עַל־נָקִי לֹא־לָקָח, עֹֽשֵׂה אֵֽלֶּה, לֹא יִמּוֹט לְעוֹלָם׃

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Consecration of a House:3
segments.html: רִבּוֹן הָעוֹלָם, הַשְׁקִֽיפָה מִמְּעוֹן קָדְשְׁךָ, וְקַבֵּל בְּרַחֲמִים וּבְרָצוֹן אֶת תְּפִלַּת בָּנֶֽיךָ וְתַחֲנוּנָם, אֲשֶׁר הִתְאַסְּפוּ פֹּה לַחֲנֹךְ אֶת הַבַּֽיִת הַזֶּה וּלְהַקְרִיב לְפָנֶֽיךָ אֶת תּוֹדָתָם עַל כָּל הַחֶֽסֶד וְהָאֱמֶת אֲשֶׁר עָשִֽׂיתָ אִתָּם. אָנָּא חַסְדְּךָ מֵאִתָּם אַל יָמוּשׁ, וּבְרִית שְׁלוֹמְךָ אַל תָּמוּט. הָגֵן בְּעַד בֵּית מְגוּרֵיהֶם, לֹא תְאֻנֶּה אֵלָיו רָעָה, וְנֶֽגַע וְצַֽעַר לֹא יִקְרְבוּ אֵלָיו, וְלֹא יִשָּׁמַע קוֹל צְוָחָה בְּתוֹכוֹ. זַכֵּה אֶת בְּנֵי הַבַּֽיִת לָשֶֽׁבֶת בְּמִשְׁכָּנָם בְּאַחֲוָה וְרֵעוּת, לְאַהֲבָה וּלְיִרְאָה אוֹתְךָ וּלְדָבְקָה בָךְ, לַהֲגוֹת בְּתוֹרָתְךָ וּלְקַיֵּם מִצְוֹתֶֽיהָ.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/Consecration of a House:5
segments.html: הָרֵק בִּרְכוֹתֶֽיךָ עַל בַּֽעַל הַבַּֽיִת. בָּרֵךְ יהוה חֵילוֹ, וּפֹֽעַל יָדָיו תִּרְצֶה׃ הַרְחִיקֵֽהוּ מִידֵי עֲבֵרָה וְעָוֹן, וִיהִי נָעֳמְךָ עָלָיו, וּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדָיו כּוֹנְנֵֽהוּ. יְהִי נָא חַסְדְּךָ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ, צוֹפִיָּה הֲלִיכוֹת בֵּיתָהּ: וְתֵדַע כִּי, אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת־יהוה הִיא תִתְהַלָּל׃ (הוֹפַע עַל בְּנֵיהֶם וּבְנוֹתֵיהֶם רֽוּחַ חָכְמָה וּבִינָה, הַדְרִיכֵם בִּנְתִיב מִצְוֹתֶֽיךָ, וְכָל־רוֹאֵיהֶם יַכִּירוּם כִּי הֵם זֶֽרַע בֵּרַךְ יהוה, בְּרוּכִים בַּתּוֹרָה וּבְיִרְאַת שָׁמַֽיִם.) שָׁמְרֵם מִכָּל רָע, שְׁמֹר אֶת נַפְשָׁם, וִיקֻיַּם בָּהֶם: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה בְּבֹאֶֽךָ, וּבָרוּךְ אַתָּה בְּצֵאתֶֽךָ: וְכַאֲשֶׁר זָכִֽינוּ לַחֲנֹךְ אֶת הַבַּֽיִת הַזֶּה עַתָּה, כֵּן נִזְכֶּה גַם יַֽחַד לִרְאוֹת חֲנֻכַּת הַבַּֽיִת הַגָּדוֹל וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בִּירוּשָׁלַֽיִם עִירְךָ, קִרְיַת מוֹעֲדֵֽינוּ, בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵֽינוּ, אָמֵן.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Consecration of a House:1
segments.html: מִזְמוֹר A psalm of David. A song for the dedication of the House. I will exalt You, <small>LORD</small>, for You have lifted me up, and not let my enemies rejoice over me. <small>LORD</small>, my God, I cried to You for help and You healed me. <small>LORD</small>, You lifted my soul from the grave; You spared me from going down to the pit. Sing to the <small>LORD</small>, you His devoted ones, and give thanks to His holy name. For His anger is for a moment, but His favor for a lifetime. At night there may be weeping, but in the morning there is joy. When I felt secure, I said, “I shall never be shaken.” <small>LORD</small>, when You favored me, You made me stand firm as a mountain, but when You hid Your face, I was terrified. To You, <small>LORD</small>, I called; I pleaded with my <small>LORD</small>: “What gain would there be if I died and went down to the grave? Can dust thank You? Can it declare Your truth? Hear, <small>LORD</small>, and be gracious to me; <small>LORD</small>, be my help.” You have turned my sorrow into dancing. You have removed my sackcloth and clothed me with joy, so that my soul may sing to You and not be silent. <small>LORD</small> my God, for ever will I thank You.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Consecration of a House:2
segments.html: מִזְמוֹר A Psalm of David. <small>LORD</small>, who may dwell in Your tent? Who may live on Your holy mountain? One who walks in integrity, does what is right, and speaks the truth from his heart; who has no malice on his tongue, does no wrong to his fellow, nor casts a slur on his neighbor; who scorns those who are vile, but honors those who fear the <small>LORD</small>; who keeps his oath even when it hurts; who does not demand interest on his loans and never takes a bribe against the innocent. One who does these things will never be shaken.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Consecration of a House:3
segments.html: רִבּוֹן הָעוֹלָם Master of the Universe, look down from Your holy dwelling place, and in compassion and favor accept the prayer and plea of Your children, who are gathered here to consecrate this house, and to offer You their thanksgiving for all the kindness and truth You have shown them. Please do let not Your kindness depart, nor Your covenant of Your peace be removed from them. Shield this their home so that no evil befalls it. May illness and sadness never come near it, nor the sound of sorrow be heard within its walls. May the members of this household live together in this home in fellowship and friendship. May they love and revere You, hold fast to You, meditating in Your Torah, and living faithfully by its commandments.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Consecration of a House:4
segments.html: Where appropriate, add the words in parentheses:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/Consecration of a House:5
segments.html: הָרֵק Bestow Your blessings on the owner of this house. <small>LORD</small> bless his resources and find favor in the work of his hands. Keep him far from sin and transgression. May Your tender love be upon him, and establish the work of our hands. May Your kindness be with his wife, she who watches over the affairs of her household, knowing that it is the God-fearing woman who deserves praise. (Bestow on their sons and daughters a spirit of wisdom and understanding. Lead them in the path of Your commandments, so that all who see them recognise that they are children blessed by the <small>LORD</small>, knowing Your Torah and revering You.) Protect them from all evil; protect their lives. May this [Your promise] be fulfilled in them: “You will be blessed when you come in, and blessed when you go out.” And as we have been able to consecrate the house, so together may we witness the consecration of the great and holy Temple in Jerusalem Your city, city of our sacred assemblies, swiftly in our days. Amen.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/The Traveler's Prayer:2
segments.html:
יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶֽיךָ, יהוה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ
שֶׁתּוֹלִיכֵֽנוּ לְשָׁלוֹם, וְתַצְעִידֵֽנוּ לְשָׁלוֹם, וְתַדְרִיכֵֽנוּ לְשָׁלוֹם
וְתַגִּיעֵֽנוּ לִמְחוֹז חֶפְצֵֽנוּ לְחַיִּים וּלְשִׂמְחָה וּלְשָׁלוֹם
(וְתַחֲזִירֵֽנוּ לְבֵיתֵֽנוּ לְשָׁלוֹם)
וְתַצִּילֵֽנוּ מִכַּף כָּל אוֹיֵב וְאוֹרֵב בַּדֶּֽרֶךְ
וּמִכָּל מִינֵי פֻּרְעָנֻיּוֹת הַמִּתְרַגְּשׁוֹת לָבוֹא לָעוֹלָם
וְתִשְׁלַח בְּרָכָה בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדֵֽינוּ
וְתִתְּנֵֽנוּ לְחֵן וּלְחֶֽסֶד וּלְרַחֲמִים בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ וּבְעֵינֵי כָל רוֹאֵֽינוּ
וְתִשְׁמַע קוֹל תַּחֲנוּנֵֽינוּ
כִּי אֵל שׁוֹמֵֽעַ תְּפִלָּה וְתַחֲנוּן אָֽתָּה.
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יהוה, שׁוֹמֵֽעַ תְּפִלָּה.

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/The Traveler's Prayer:3
segments.html: יהוה יִשְׁמָר־צֵאתְךָ וּבוֹאֶֽךָ, מֵעַתָּה וְעַד־עוֹלָם׃

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/The Traveler's Prayer:5
segments.html:
וְיַעֲקֹב הָלַךְ לְדַרְכּוֹ, וַיִּפְגְּעוּ־בוֹ מַלְאֲכֵי אֱלֹהִים׃
וַיֹּֽאמֶר יַעֲקֹב כַּאֲשֶׁר רָאָם, מַחֲנֵה אֱלֹהִים זֶה
וַיִּקְרָא שֵׁם־הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא מַחֲנָֽיִם׃

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/The Traveler's Prayer:7
segments.html:
יְבָרֶכְךָ יהוה וְיִשְׁמְרֶֽךָ׃
יָאֵר יהוה פָּנָיו אֵלֶֽיךָ וִיחֻנֶּֽךָּ׃
יִשָּׂא יהוה פָּנָיו אֵלֶֽיךָ וְיָשֵׂם לְךָ שָׁלוֹם׃

segments.id: he:Giving Thanks/The Traveler's Prayer:8
segments.html: שִׁיר לַמַּעֲלוֹת, אֶשָּׂא עֵינַי אֶל־הֶהָרִים, מֵאַֽיִן יָבֹא עֶזְרִי׃ עֶזְרִי מֵעִם יהוה, עֹשֵׂה שָׁמַֽיִם וָאָֽרֶץ׃ אַל־יִתֵּן לַמּוֹט רַגְלֶֽךָ, אַל־יָנוּם שֹׁמְרֶֽךָ׃ הִנֵּה לֹא־יָנוּם וְלֹא יִישָׁן, שׁוֹמֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל׃ יהוה שֹׁמְרֶֽךָ, יהוה צִלְּךָ עַל־יַד יְמִינֶֽךָ׃ יוֹמָם הַשֶּֽׁמֶשׁ לֹא־יַכֶּֽכָּה, וְיָרֵֽחַ בַּלָּֽיְלָה׃ יהוה יִשְׁמָרְךָ מִכָּל־רָע, יִשְׁמֹר אֶת־נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃ יהוה יִשְׁמָר־צֵאתְךָ וּבוֹאֶֽךָ, מֵעַתָּה וְעַד־עוֹלָם׃

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/The Traveler's Prayer:1
segments.html: If one intends to return home on the same day, add the words in parentheses:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/The Traveler's Prayer:2
segments.html:
יְהִי רָצוֹן May it be Your will,
LORD our God and God of our fathers,
to lead us to peace, direct our steps to peace,
guide us to peace, and bring us to our desired destination in life, joy and peace
(and bring us back to our home in peace).
Rescue us from any enemy or ambush on the way,
and from all afflictions that trouble the world.
Send blessing to the work of our hands,
and let us find grace, kindness and compassion
from You and from all who see us.
Hear our pleas,
for You are a God who hears prayer and pleas.
Blessed are You, LORD, who listens to prayer.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/The Traveler's Prayer:3
segments.html: May the <small>LORD</small> guard your going out and your return, from now and for all time.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/The Traveler's Prayer:4
segments.html: Repeat three times:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/The Traveler's Prayer:5
segments.html:
וְיַעֲקֹב And Jacob went on his way and angels of God met him.
When he saw them, Jacob said, “This is God’s camp”
and he named the place Maḥanaim [two camps].

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/The Traveler's Prayer:6
segments.html: Repeat three times:

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/The Traveler's Prayer:7
segments.html:
יְבָרֶכְךָ May the LORD bless you and protect you.
May the LORD make His face shine on you and be gracious to you.
May the LORD turn His face toward you and grant you peace.

segments.id: en:Giving Thanks/The Traveler's Prayer:8
segments.html: שִׁיר לַמַּעֲלוֹת A song of ascents. I lift my eyes up to the hills; from where will my help come? My help comes from the <small>LORD</small>, Maker of heaven and earth. He will not let your foot stumble; He who guards you does not slumber. See: the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps. The <small>LORD</small> is your Guardian; the <small>LORD</small> is your Shade at your right hand. The sun will not strike you by day, nor the moon by night. The <small>LORD</small> will guard you from all harm; He will guard your life. The <small>LORD</small> will guard your going and coming, now and for evermore.
